prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right choice depends on your priorities (price, speed, quality, eco-friendly paints, warranty) and your home’s needs. I don’t have live local review data, but I can help you find the best fit. Quick options and next steps:

What I can do now
- Give a shortlist of highly rated national brands that operate in St. Louis (e.g., CertaPro Painters, Five Star Painting) and suggest searching local listings for independent contractors.
- Give a checklist and questions to use when comparing painters.
- Give typical cost ranges and red flags.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and priorities (budget vs. premium finish, timeline, rooms and square footage, need for repairs) and I’ll narrow options and draft an email/text you can send for quotes.

How to choose the best interior painter
1. Use multiple sources: check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the Better Business Bureau. Look for companies with many recent 4–5 star reviews and responses to complaints.
2. Verify credentials: insurance (liability + workers’ comp), business license if required locally, and ask for references from recent local jobs.
3. Get at least 3 written estimates that include: prep work (patching, sanding, priming), number of coats, paint brand & sheen, number of painters, start/completion dates, cleanup and disposal, and warranty.
4. Compare apples-to-apples: cheaper bids may skip prep or use lower-grade paint.
5. Ask for portfolio photos of completed interior jobs similar to yours (age/style of home, trim work, ceilings).
6. Confirm cleanup and protection: floor/tape protection, moving furniture, and dust control.

Questions to ask each painter
- Are you insured and can you provide proof?
- How many years have you been doing interior painting?
- What brand/line of paint do you recommend and why?
- How do you handle prep work and repairs?
- Will there be a written contract and warranty? What does it cover?
- Can you provide local references or recent job photos?
- What is the timeline for our job?

Typical cost guidance (St. Louis-range estimates)
- Per square foot (interior walls): roughly $1.50–$3.50/ft² depending on prep and paint.
- Per standard room: roughly $300–$1,000 each (small bedroom at low end; large rooms or high ceilings at high end).
- Expect higher costs for extensive drywall repair, textured ceilings, or specialty finishes.

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or references.
- Very low bid with vague scope (no prep, no paint brand listed).
- High-pressure tactics to sign immediately.
- Demands full payment up front.

If you want specific company recommendations, provide your ZIP code and any preferences (budget, eco paints, timeline) and I’ll give a short list of top-rated local options and a message template you can use to request quotes.
